title: Identifying the Banner Band photograph
summary: Russell and Duhé go through the Banner Band photograph, naming Bunk Johnson, Gus Fortinet, E.T. Thomas and the rest.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, it can't be the I'm showing you with a couple. I don't care where you're coming from. Well, we were talking about Louie a minute ago. Where do you think he got his style? From Oliver or from Bunk? When did you play with Bunk? You say first in the Eagle Band a little bit way back? Then we went to Noir and Lyrie. Can you tell me about that Banner Band, because I don't know much about that. Well, there's a cut in there. So that picture, just a minute, let me see if I can find that. And you can mention who's in that. Oh, yeah, sure. Because Bunk doesn't even look natural to me.
He's a young Bunk. I don't know if you keep him from drinking. That one was in the Banner Band. I don't know if you keep Bunk from drinking.

And who is the trombone player? The trombone, that's Gus Fortnay. Oh, I met him then, sure. Sure. At Bunk's funeral, he was there. Yeah, sure. And I stopped later on the way home. And he played at the town down a little bit farther. I met Gus, yeah. I forgot his last name. Gus Fortnay. And that's Bunk. And then who's the? Evan Thomas. And the drummer? Robert Stafford. Stafford. Drummer. You say he's in California now?

Oh, he's still in New Iberia. Or the piano. He's in Los Angeles. William Boyner. Burnham? B-R-N-E-R. Burner. Yeah. Burner. Oh, I knew something like that. Burner played sax. A friend of Dink Johnson. Did you ever know Bill Johnson and Dink Johnson? I know Dink. I know Dink Johnson. He's dead now, too. That's Ed Reedom. He's dead. The banjo is Ed Reedom.
And the tenor sax. Tenor sax.
And this is you. That's me. And the album? That's Classe Roy. Classe Roy. Played in third sax. Third sax.
Classe Roy. Roy. R-O-Y. R-O-Y. And who's the bass player? John Sandis. John Sandis. That was a big band. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
